outcomes.text: Apply AI methods and tools to new problems in a chosen discipline.
Choose appropriate AI tools for different problems.
Assess professional responsibilities and the societal benefits and risks of AI applications.

courses.name: The Digital Revolution: Computer and Data Science For All
courses.description: Introduces computing and data science, their history and societal effects, with a Python laboratory.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: No previous enrollment in a 300-level CSDS course. The recommended pre-requisite is comfort with high school algebra.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence for All Disciplines
courses.description: Introduces AI and machine learning through practical tools for disciplinary problems and discussion of social and ethical implications.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: ( CSDS 101 or CSDS 132 or ECSE 132 or CSDS 134 or DESN 210 or ENGR 131 ) and no current or previous enrollment in a 300-level CSDS course.

courses.name: Current Issues in Artificial Intelligence, For Better or Worse
courses.description: Examines autonomous decisions, generative tools, technical failure modes, and policy responses through an interdisciplinary seminar.
courses.prerequisites: The class is open to all majors, but students should have a strong background in engineering, science, or computer technology.

courses.name: Responsible AI: Cultivating a Just and Sustainable Socio-technical Future through Data Citizenship
courses.description: Studies responsible AI through hands-on examination of data practices, collective responsibility, and a data citizenship project.

courses.name: The Politics of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Uses political philosophy and philosophy of technology to examine AI infrastructure, institutions, and political decisions.

courses.name: Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology
courses.description: Examines automation, bias, autonomy, accountability, and responsible AI design through ethical debate.

courses.name: Applying Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain in Business and Finance
courses.description: Evaluates practical AI and blockchain business uses, their limitations, and questions to ask before adopting them.

courses.name: Financial Data Science: Data Analytics & Machine Learning Fundamentals
courses.description: Uses SQL and Python to prepare financial data, build supervised models, and evaluate predictive performance.

courses.name: Financial Modeling
courses.description: Builds linked financial statements and valuation models in Excel, including sensitivity and scenario analysis.

courses.name: Corporate Risk Management
courses.description: Studies financial and other corporate risks, measurement techniques, derivatives, and strategic risk management.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: MBAP 405 or MBAC 504 or MBAC 505 .

courses.name: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence in Business Analytics
courses.description: Applies regression, classification, model selection, neural networks, trees, kernels, and clustering to business analytics.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq or Coreq: BUAI/MSBA 434 or BUAI/MSBA 444. Prereq: Master of Business Analytics & Intelligence students only and (BUAI/MSBA 492 or SCMG/MSOR 492 or BTEC 420 ).

courses.name: Cognition and Computation
courses.description: Connects theories and models of human cognition with computational analysis, AI, and empirical datasets.

courses.name: Advanced Econometrics
courses.description: Extends regression to causal analysis using panel data, instruments, quasi-experiments, and treatment evaluation.

courses.name: Economics of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Platforms
courses.description: Examines AI’s economic effects and digital platforms while practicing critical verification of AI-generated analysis.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: ECON 102 AND ( ANTH 319 or OPRE 207 or SOCI 307 or STAT 201 or STAT 301 or STAT 312 ).

courses.name: Computational Methods for Economic Modeling
courses.description: Uses algorithms, simulation, and computational optimization to model economic mechanisms and dynamic systems.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: ECON 102 and ( OPRE 207 or ANTH 319 or SOCI 307 or STAT 201 or STAT 301 or STAT 312 ).

courses.name: Machine Learning for Predictive Analytics in Economics
courses.description: Builds economic prediction workflows from data preparation through supervised learning, clustering, forecasting, and communication.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: ECON 102 and ( ANTH 319 or OPRE 207 or SOCI 307 or STAT 301 or STAT 312 ).

courses.name: Algorithmic Trading
courses.description: Develops and evaluates algorithmic trading strategies using market data, statistical learning, and text analysis.
courses.prerequisites: Coding experience required or consent of instructor required.

courses.name: Coding for the Humanities: Python, Natural Language Processing, and Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces Python and language processing for humanities text analysis through computational experimentation and critical reflection.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Healthcare Management
courses.description: Introduces deep learning for healthcare management, with applications, adoption challenges, and limitations.

courses.name: AI in Medicine: Knowledge Representation and Deep Learning
courses.description: Covers biomedical knowledge models, natural language processing, and large-scale data technologies through readings and a team project.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science for Social Impact
courses.description: Uses social-policy cases to introduce prediction, causal inference, and ethical stewardship of data.

courses.name: Semester Research Project in Data Science for Social Impact
courses.description: Develops a reproducible social-impact research project using R, staged peer feedback, and ethical data practices.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals for Supply Chain Management
courses.description: Applies machine learning and deep learning to supply-chain problems with Python exercises and attention to responsible implementation.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: SCMG 433 and SCMG 492 and enrolled in the Master of Supply Chain Management program.

courses.name: Case Studies in Artificial Intelligence - Supply Chain Applications
courses.description: Examines supply-chain digitization cases across planning, procurement, distribution, manufacturing, and services.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: SCMG 492 and enrolled in the Master of Supply Chain Management program.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence for Biomedical Research
courses.description: Applies and evaluates AI models for biomedical questions through projects addressing biological data and ethical concerns.
courses.prerequisites: Prereq: ( SYBB 402 and SYBB 411 ) or SYBB 412 .

requirements.title: AI Application Electives
requirements.summary: Choose at least 2 listed courses totaling at least 6 published credits.

requirements.title: University minor policy
requirements.summary: A signed minor declaration must be submitted and recorded in SIS; the requirements term normally follows matriculation unless a later catalog is selected. Minor changes/corrections should be submitted at least one semester before graduation. External coursework needs advance approval, including department approval for the minor, an official transcript, and a grade of C or better; no grade-point average is imported from the external course.

requirements.title: University minor policy
requirements.summary: Minor courses require regular evaluative grades. Elected pass/no-pass courses do not count, except courses officially designated pass/no-pass-only in SIS. A later-declared minor may permit a request to reveal an earlier elected pass/no-pass grade at the start of the final academic term.

requirements.title: Eligibility and preparation
requirements.summary: Available to all undergraduate students. No prior computing experience or knowledge is assumed or required.

requirements.title: Required foundation enrollment restrictions
requirements.summary: No previous enrollment in a 300-level CSDS course. Comfort with high-school algebra is recommended.

requirements.title: Required foundation enrollment restrictions
requirements.summary: CSDS 101, CSDS 132, ECSE 132, CSDS 134, DESN 210 or ENGR 131; no current or previous enrollment in a 300-level CSDS course.

requirements.title: Listed electives with graduate enrollment restrictions
requirements.summary: The minor lists BUAI 446 and SCMG 462/463 as options, but their course catalogs restrict enrollment to the relevant master’s program. BUAI 446 specifies Master of Business Analytics & Intelligence students only; SCMG 462/463 require enrollment in Master of Supply Chain Management. No undergraduate exception was verified. See the course records and SCMG course source; listing is not a waiver.

requirements.title: Course requisites and career permission process
requirements.summary: Unmet course conditions require an approved requisites override. Cross-career restrictions may additionally require permission from the student or course school registrar/dean. Approval does not enroll the student automatically. This general process is not evidence of a blanket undergraduate exception for BUAI 446 or SCMG 462/463; their named master-program restrictions remain unresolved for this minor.

notes: This Applied Artificial Intelligence minor is distinct from the university Artificial Intelligence minor. No technical-minor overlap cap or prerequisites are inherited.

The 2026–2027 bulletin publishes the full minor while the undated university AI hub still labels it NEW, In Approval. Current activity is unknown pending reconciliation; publication does not establish first instruction.
Course units follow the independently reviewed university semester-based credit definition. Cross-listed and combined-level labels are each preserved as one published choice.

The published local minor requirements and university declaration/transfer/grading conditions are mapped. Inventory status is partial because graduate-only elective eligibility conflicts remain unresolved; course metadata gaps are separate.
The introductory courses restrict prior/current advanced CSDS enrollment. CSDS 102 prerequisite alternatives do not waive the separately required CSDS 101 minor course.

All 25 published course options have reviewed catalog descriptions and individual amounts. ECON 334/380/381, MBAP 429H and SCMG 462/463 are 1.5 semester hours each; two options alone may not satisfy the separate six-hour application minimum. Graduate-only restrictions on BUAI 446 and SCMG 462/463 are preserved; the minor listing supplies no verified exception.

Course-search endpoints were robots-disallowed on 2026-10-10. Independently linked public department directories were robots-permitted and fetched successfully. Catalog Units are normalized using the separately reviewed semester-based credit-hour definition. No term-specific syllabus or public class site was verified in this pass.

Registrar policy permits requests to override requisites and career restrictions, with separate school administrator review where applicable. The public procedure does not establish an approved undergraduate path for the three named graduate-restricted electives. No SIS login, permission request or contact with university staff was attempted.
